statement: >= 15 distinct organisations have a training run >= 1e26 FLOP (Epoch AI; snapshot 2027-12-31)
status_at_phase_end: 0 organisations known to have a >= 1e26 FLOP run by end-2023. The largest publicly estimated run was ~2e25 FLOP (a Bloc A developer's GPT-4, per Epoch), roughly 5x below the threshold; a second Bloc A developer released a new flagship model family in Dec 2023 with no disclosed compute. A Bloc A executive order (Oct 2023) adopted 1e26 operations as a reporting trigger, showing the threshold was then regarded as beyond existing models.

items.summary: Epoch AI analysis of industry labs: the most compute-intensive known run was a Bloc A developer's flagship model at an estimated 2e25 FLOP; a few Bloc A firms dominate frontier compute, and Bloc B labs lag on all metrics.
items.detail: Epoch AI, 'Who is leading in AI? An analysis of industry AI research' (late 2023; publication date approximate) (verified via web_extract this run): Google ~10-million-fold compute growth over 11 years, OpenAI and Meta ~1-million-fold in six years; GPT-4 ~2e25 FLOP; Bloc B labs trail Bloc A labs.

items.summary: A Bloc A executive order set interim reporting triggers for dual-use foundation models trained with > 1e26 operations and for clusters with > 1e20 operations per second, i.e. above every model then known.
items.detail: Bloc A Executive Order 14110, Sec. 4.2(b)-(c), 88 FR 75191, published 2023-11-01 (signed 2023-10-30) (verified via web_extract of the Federal Register full text this run: cluster threshold 1e20 ops/s and 1e26-operation model trigger in 4.2(c)(iii)).

items.summary: A second Bloc A developer launched a new flagship multimodal model family in three sizes, trained on its in-house accelerators; training compute was not disclosed.
items.detail: Google, 'Introducing Gemini: our largest and most capable AI model', 2023-12-06 (verified via web_extract this run): Ultra/Pro/Nano, trained on TPU v4 and v5e. No FLOP figure published in-phase.
